messages:
alix: FYI CI blocked on PR feature/regen-stability — typegen job produced a regen diff that only reorders changelog arrays and flips README example lines. Semver guard treats it as a surface change.

rhea: ugh. looks like docs-only noise but the guard is strict. which generator area?

regen-bot: pipeline: typegen #5099 failed (exit 1). Artifact: /artifacts/typegen/2955001111/regendiff.log

tom: pasted snippet from regendiff:
```diff
-  - highlights: ["fast-start", "migrations"]
+  - highlights: ["migrations", "fast-start"]
```

nina: Also saw that python README shows `retry: 3` while ts README shows `retry: 2` after regen — SDK parity tests flip based on that doc snippet which causes sampleapp flaky failures.

alix: Two immediate proposals: (A) relax semver guard so docs-only diffs (changelogs, README snippets, examples) are WARN not FAIL; show warning in release UI. (B) add a cheap regen-idempotence CI job for PRs touching generators/specs: run regen twice and assert clean.

rhea: agree. Short-term WARN would unblock releases and keep reviewer attention. Long-term we fix generator determinism.

tom: I'll open a small PR to canonicalize $ref traversal order and normalize arrays for changelog metadata in the generator output. Should reduce noise.

nina: I'll add a DX parity check that diffs auth/retry code blocks across generated SDK READMEs and fails CI if they diverge. And I'll add the double-regen idempotence job gated to generator/spec PRs.

alix: Filing an incident to unstick the release and track follow-ups: https://redwood-internal/ops/INC-2042-regendiff-noise. Will manually allow this publish once semver-guard->WARN patch is merged. :white_check_mark:

rhea: can we also add a unit test that runs regen on a minimal anyOf schema to catch ordering non-determinism?

tom: yep, adding an idempotence unit test to the generator test-suite now.

nina: sounds good. thanks team — let's aim to land both patches today so we don't pile more releases behind this. :rocket:
